water.title: The Water Blind Spot
water.blurb: Your biggest avoidable exposure is coming through your glass — unfiltered or bottled water can carry disinfection by-products, trace metals, PFAS and microplastics.
water.fix: Add a certified water filter (carbon or reverse-osmosis) and drink from glass or steel. It's the highest-value single upgrade for most people.

air.title: The Indoor-Air Load
air.blurb: You spend most of your day breathing indoor air, and yours is carrying more particulate and VOCs than it needs to — from cooking, combustion or traffic.
air.fix: Ventilate while cooking and add a correctly sized HEPA purifier to your main room. Cut scented candles and plug-ins. Air is the exposure you control most.

plastic.title: The Plastic-to-Food Pipeline
plastic.blurb: Heat plus plastic is quietly the leakiest exposure in your kitchen — heating and storing food in plastic drives migration of plastics and additives into what you eat.
plastic.fix: Never microwave or store hot food in plastic. Switch to glass or ceramic, and retire scratched nonstick pans for cast iron or stainless.

food.title: The Dietary Exposure Pattern
food.blurb: Your food choices are adding avoidable load — from pesticide residue, mercury in large fish, or the additives and packaging that come with ultra-processed food.
food.fix: Buy organic for the few high-residue crops (berries, greens), choose small fish over large predators, and shift toward whole foods. Wash produce well — it's free.

care.title: The Personal-Care Stack
care.blurb: Fragrance and a long product routine mean you're absorbing a daily cocktail of undisclosed 'parfum' and preservatives through your skin.
care.fix: Go fragrance-free where you can and simplify your routine. Fewer products means fewer unknowns — one of the easiest cuts to make.

home.title: The Household-Chemical Background
home.blurb: Your home environment — cleaning sprays, scented laundry, or an untested radon risk — is adding a background exposure you rarely notice.
home.fix: Switch to fragrance-free or DIY cleaning basics, drop dryer sheets, and get a one-time radon test if you have ground-contact living space.

balanced.title: The Low-Exposure Baseline
balanced.blurb: Impressive — your avoidable environmental exposures are already low. Your body's own detox systems aren't fighting much of an uphill battle.
balanced.fix: Pick your lowest-scoring answer above and tighten just that one lever. Then focus on consistency: clean water, clean air, less heated plastic.
